title: Weather
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Lightning and floods are real dangers in many parts of Kenya: teach the safe action first (SAFE).

skills.key_step: The child describes unfavourable weather, says how it can harm people and what to do to stay safe.

floor.question: What is the weather when the sky is dark and water falls?

representations: pictures of a flood, a storm, a drought, hail
a "what do I do?" card for each
steps: Name the weather in the picture.
Say how it can hurt people.
contexts: a drought in a dry area

board.do: Draw a storm with lightning and a tall tree.

board.say: Is it safe to stand here?

board.do: Wait for the child to say no and where to go.
Write: go indoors, not under a tree.

misconceptions.ask: It starts to thunder and rain while you walk home. Where do you go?
misconceptions.repair: Show that lightning strikes the tallest thing. Practise going into a building or crouching low in the open.

misconceptions.ask: A small river is flooded up to your knees on the way to school. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Show how a little moving water can push over a child. Rule: turn back, wait for an adult.

misconceptions.ask: Can very hot weather be dangerous?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about a drought: dry rivers, dying crops and thirst. Name the safe actions: water, shade, hat.

misconceptions.ask: You hear thunder but it is not raining yet. Can you keep playing football in the field?
misconceptions.repair: Teach the rule: when thunder roars, go indoors. Lightning can strike before the rain.

checks.question: What do you do when you hear thunder?
